tutorial.title: Tutorial
tutorial.whatIsThisBody: Pythomics is a desktop application for running multi-omics integration pipelines without needing to write code. It is a Python port of the R mixOmics library (Bioconductor), preserving the same numerical precision and the same algorithms.
tutorial.localNote: The statistical computation runs 100% locally. In future versions, with explicit consent, public biological APIs (UniProt, MyGene) may be queried to annotate biomarkers, and LLM services may be used to assist the preliminary analysis. In those cases only generic identifiers (gene, protein and metabolite names) and aggregate metrics are sent — never sample values or concrete study information.
tutorial.step1: Load your data. Upload one or more .csv or .tsv files with your matrices (gene expression, proteomics, metabolomics or clinical variables). Rows are samples and columns are variables.
tutorial.step2: Configure the model. Choose the analysis type (PCA, sPLS-DA, DIABLO, …) and the main parameters (number of components, keepX).
tutorial.step3: <emphasis>Visualize the results.</emphasis> Get plots and a table of selected biomarkers. Export figures and reports for your research.
tutorial.whereToStartBody: You can try one of the example datasets bundled with mixOmics. No internet connection or extra configuration is needed.
tutorial.moreInfoBody: To learn in detail about the statistical models, their parameters and assumptions, as well as the different visualizations, you can consult the official documentation of the mixOmics library:

exampleDataset.nutrimouse.description: 40 mice with gene expression + lipidomics. Classified by genotype (Wild-type / PPARα) and diet (Cocoa butter / Sunflower oil).
exampleDataset.srbct.description: 63 pediatric tumors (Small Round Blue Cell Tumors): 4 classes (Ewing sarcoma, neuroblastoma, etc.) with 2308 genes.
exampleDataset.breast_TCGA.description: 150 breast cancer samples with 3 omics (miRNA, mRNA, protein). 4 molecular subtypes. Avance case study for DIABLO.
